'''Proof of liquidity''' (PoL) is a design that pays people for '''providing liquidity''' rather than for holding a token, and measures that liquidity with a token of its own. The idea is adapted from Berachain. On [[PRANA Blockchain|PRANA]] the proof-of-liquidity token is [[MWALI]].

== The problem it solves ==

A reward token with no liquidity is a number on a screen. Someone holding it cannot sell it, price it, or borrow against it, because there is no pool deep enough to trade into. Most token designs treat liquidity as something that will show up by itself, or rent it temporarily with emissions aimed at whoever is passing.

Proof of liquidity makes the opposite assumption: liquidity is the scarce thing, so it should be the thing that is measured and rewarded.

== The separation ==

The key move is to split two rewards that are usually the same token:

* '''The reward token''' — on PRANA, [[KulaSwap|KULA]]. Emission-only, capped, and paid for a variety of activity.
* '''The proof-of-liquidity token''' — [[MWALI]]. Minted only by a gauge, only to people who have actually supplied liquidity to a designated pair.

Keeping them separate means a liquidity position becomes a first-class, measurable, governance-relevant thing. It can be counted, voted with, paired back, or wired into further gauges, without diluting the reward token's own emission schedule.

== Gauges ==

A '''gauge''' is the contract that meters this. Liquidity providers stake their pool position in the gauge, and the gauge mints the proof-of-liquidity token to them over time. A '''gauge controller''' sits above the gauges and directs how much emission each pool receives, which is what makes the question "which pools should this economy pay for?" into a governance decision rather than a fixed constant.

On PRANA the designated pair is KULA/WPRANA — the "Kula-Ring" — which ties issuance to the depth of the pool that actually backs the reward token.

== Why no human can print it ==

By design, the proof-of-liquidity token has no human minter. The gauge holds the only minting role; the deployer holds none and has renounced its administrative role, leaving administration with the DAO timelock. The token therefore cannot be printed by a person — only emitted by the mechanism, to people who supplied liquidity.

== Status on PRANA ==

The contracts are deployed, but '''proof of liquidity is not yet emitting'''. The KULA/WPRANA gauge's configured reward token is KULA, not MWALI, and MWALI's total supply is zero — it has never been minted. Until the gauge is repointed, liquidity providers are earning the reward token rather than the proof-of-liquidity token, and MWALI exists on paper only. The gauge's administration sits behind a two-day timelock, so correcting it is a governance action with a delay, not a quick fix.

This is recorded here rather than glossed over, because the difference between a design and a running system is the entire point of writing any of this down.
